newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond and interest rate futures settled little changed on Tuesday after a relatively quiet session with traders viewing the latest polls showing a narrowing of the gap between the left and right with caution.

Traders said there was still a belief the centre-right coalition would retain power and a reluctance to take the polls too seriously given the fact they were wide of the mark during the 1995 presidential elections.
The options pits were active however, with 16,000 puts on the bond future at 127 and 11,000 at 128 traded. Out of the money puts in the June PIBOR were also the most heavily traded.
An options trader said investors were looking to take advantage of a possible decline in the French market amid the current ongoing political uncertainty.
Joanne Perez, strategist at Merrill Lynch in Paris said, however, the risk of the French market whipsawing on the back of conflicting polls was keeping some on the sidelines.
She said investors may be more likely to start taking positions in the week before the election when it is forbidden under French law for polls to be published.
A futures trader at a French bank "sooner or later, (the election) it will impact if the majority keeps contracting."
Traders said investors were starting to put on curve flattening trades on the grounds that if more of a risk premium were priced into French assets the short end of the curve would be hit most.
The gap between two- and 10-year French bonds narrowed three basis points on Tuesday after a similar move on Monday. The 10-year spread with Bunds was steady at minus seven.

Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro, said the switch by most market participants to the July 2007 Bund from the January 2007 Bund to calculate the spread understated the extent of the French underperformance recently.
He said the spread had narrowed from minus 15 to about minus four basis points since the election was called using the same two French and German bonds for both calculations.
The franc was steady at 3.3747 per mark.
